h1: Roadmap planning for the months after launch
overview: Once your product is live, everything feels urgent. We sit down with you, look at your feedback, usage numbers and goals, and decide what to build next and what to leave. You get a roadmap in plain language with three time horizons, a reason for every item and a rough effort estimate, so you can keep the team focused and say no to distractions with confidence.

faq: What data do you need to plan a roadmap?
Whatever you have: feedback messages, support emails, sign-up numbers or notes from user calls. If you have little, we say so and plan around the questions you still need to answer.
Is this the same as product scoping?
No. Scoping defines a first version before it exists. Roadmap planning is for products that are already live or about to be, and decides the order of improvements using real user signals.
Will you commit to a delivery date for each item?
We give effort estimates as ranges and flag the risks, not promises. Dates depend on your team's capacity. If we build the work, we confirm timing in a written fixed price quote.
Which format do I receive the roadmap in?
A shareable page or document, plus a spreadsheet version if you prefer to track it yourself. It uses plain labels, so teammates and investors can read it without a briefing.
